This Woven Kingdom #2

Uneltiri fără sfârșit

Tahereh Mafi, Ioana Bena (Translator)

4.09
80,910 ratings13,614 reviews
Rate this book
Goodreads Choice Award
Nominee for Readers' Favorite Young Adult Fantasy & Science Fiction (2023)
În focul unui sărut, zidurile dintre Alizeh, moștenitoarea de mult pierdută a unui străvechi regat al djinnilor, și Kamran, prințul moștenitor al imperiului Arduniei, s-au prăbușit. Și la fel și viețile celor doi. Bunicul lui Kamran, regele Arduniei, zace mort, iar îngrozitorul secret al pactului său cu diavolul a fost dat în vileag în fața lumii întregi.

Cyrus, misteriosul rege cu părul arămiu, a răpit-o pe Alizeh și a dus-o în Tulan, regatul vecin peste care stăpânește. Suveranul a încheiat și el propria înțelegere cu diavolul, care ar presupune ca tânăra să-și trădeze sentimentele pentru Kamran dacă vrea să-și revendice tronul djinnilor. Aceasta însă nu vrea să aibă nimic de-a face cu Cyrus sau cu pactul lui cu Iblees.

Fără nicio posibilitate de a fugi din Tulan și cu promisiunea tentantă de a-și împlini destinul de moștenitoare a tronului djinnilor, Alizeh este silită să se întrebe dacă își poate lăsa emoțiile deoparte și, în cele din urmă, să devină suverana de care supușii ei au nevoie. Între timp, Kamran încearcă să își salveze regatul distrus. Confruntându-se cu trădarea la fiecare pas, tot ce știe sigur este că trebuie să meargă în Tulan pentru a-și răzbuna bunicul.

Și nu poate decât să spere că Alizeh îl va aștepta acolo și că nu a devenit încă stăpâna acelui regat.

About the author

Tahereh Mafi

82 books78.2k followers
Tahereh Mafi is the New York Times and USA Today bestselling author of the Shatter Me series. She was born in a small city somewhere in Connecticut and currently resides in Santa Monica, California with her husband, fellow author Ransom Riggs. She can usually be found over-caffeinated and stuck in a book. Shatter Me is her first series, with television rights optioned by ABC Signature Studios; Furthermore, her first middle grade novel, is on shelves now, and Whichwood, its darker companion, will be on shelves November 14, 2017.

She put her everything in to this book. It was so good!! The plot was minimised and nothing much happened in the book truth be told, the story was progressing but not as fast as I thought but I had no problem with that 😭 because the vibes and everything were perfect!! It was so fun to read like not once was I bored. I was hooked and I honestly wanted more and I couldn't get enough of it. I think almost nothing of that much significant in terms of the actual big plot was made but the characters contributions to that plot was very significant and it overall was very well written.

The writing style in this series is so much different from her writing style in shatter me and I must admit I prefer this one to that because it's so beautiful and so easy and fun to read. It's actually very beautifully written. I love the change and it reads more like a fantasy book which is what I said for the first book as well!!

“She saw an intensity in his stunning irises, something desperate straining against his control, and she swore in that moment she could almost feel his soul pressing against hers.”

Alizeh is the type of FMC who won't back down. She's so much better than most of the female characters present in fantasies or romantasies because she doesn't whine, she has a backbone and she stands up for herself. I love how she's so polite 😭 that even when she's angry she argues in a polite way 😭 it's actually very cute this book was easily characters driven and it reflected a lot on alizehs arc because we got to know so much from her side, more of her magic, her history and her powers and they were so needed like I was desperate to know 😭 also I love how tahereh was foreshadowing stuff all along 🤭

“You have no idea what I want. I have been in agony for eight months, Alizeh. Do you know how hard it’s been to pretend I don’t know you? To pretend I don’t want you? To act as if I haven’t known every inch of your body in my dreams? To learn that your heart has been entangled elsewhere? I look at you and I can’t breathe. In my mind, you are already mine.”

Cyrus? The ginger haired man who begged Alizeh to be her bride, was willing to give her his entire kingdom and for her to kill him and confessed his feelings when having hurt? That Cyrus?? HE STOLE THE WHOLE BOOK with his presence. I love him so much and I'm afraid I'm not willing to open my ears for any slander regarding him.

Is he perfect? No.
Is he going to be potentially one of my favourite morally grey characters? Yes.
Is he also one of the most downbad and shameless flirts I've met? Yes.

I think I understand why Tahereh gave so much time to the characters rather than the plot in this one considering how book 1 ended and with Cyrus only appearing in the second half as a stranger who we knew nothing about. It was important to give him more page time and to explore his character in depth. I absolutely loved his scenes and I' want to know more because he is a very conflicting character.

Am I being dramatic by rating this a 4.5? PROBABLY. But I just feel so giddy, and this did everything I expect a YA fantasy romance to do 😂
From the very start of this book, picking up straight from where we left off in the first one - I was immediately LOCKED IN.

I do just love Alizeh as our protagonist. She is the perfect balance of having strength of her own, being able to take care of herself and stand up for herself - but at the same time, choosing to not be just a feral creature 99% of the time. We see her softer side as well, her caring side and also her naivety - and I love seeing the duality in her character.

I'm still loving the melodrama of it all. Tahereh Mafi's old school classic romance writing style just leans into ALL of the drama & yearning, and I just love it all.

Without saying too much... I do LOVE our new character that we get to know in this book 👀
And while this book maybe didn't have the fastest moving plot, I loved getting to know our characters more, and seeing their relationships form.

Dragons, mythical creatures, what more could I ask for really? I feel like this series is sort of the perfect mix of the Cassandra Clare Shadowhunters books and Stephanie Garber's OUABH. Excited to read on and see where our plot goes, and ALSO happy to see the beginnings of a misfit found family...

Hehe.

i implore tahereh mafi to take a break from writing either thirty fifth sequel to shatter me or the needlessly stretched out this woven kingdom series and take a creative writing class instead. although i was not blown away by this woven kingdom - the first book in the series - i nonetheless decided to read book 2, in hopes that the issues from the previous installment would be fixed here. alas, not only was that not the case, these infinite threads was infinitely worse.

i guess i should start with the elephant in the room, which is the pacing of the story. now, this problem already existed in the previous book, but here it was greatly exacerbated. the entirety of the novel - more than 400 pages for me - happened within 24 hours. this in itself is not the issue; there are some stories that are told in the same timeframe but work splendidly. however, that is not the case when one considers the plot advancements and the character developments that are offered here. the writing leads us to believe that certain characters have gone from point a to point z in terms of their views and emotions, but the moment we stop to think about these things for more than 3 seconds, this “logic” starts to crumble. for instance, it is completely unbelievable that a character can go from wholeheartedly hating someone to all within less than 1 day.

on a somewhat related note, another issue here is the writing style. it may be one of the most severe cases of purple prose i have come across in the fantasy genre. it seems to me that with this book tahereh mafi was trying to overcompensate for the atrocity that was shatter me (writing-wise in this case, but this applies to all of the other aspects of that book to be honest), and the book suffers immensely as a result. i mentioned this in my review for this woven kingdom, but it bothered me so much here as well that i felt the need to reiterate my point once again. ms mafi, there are other, better ways to show your readers that you have grown as an author, and they dont involve the most ostentatious, tedious prose known to man.

as a result of the issues mentioned just now, the rest of the book falls flat, starting with the characters. here i have so many things to say that i am at a loss as to where to start. i guess before i go off on a tangent, it would be prudent to mention that i skipped all of kamran’s povs, because of how immensely annoying and boring he was as a character. i tried to force myself to skim through his chapters, at least, to understand what his storyline represents for the plot overall (which is nonexistent by the way, but i will get to that later), but then i realized they say nothing of value so i stopped trying. there is absolutely nothing of interest about this character that hasnt been done before. it is bad enough that he is a badly written character, but he is also something worse than that: boring and annoying.

the situation for alizeh, who is supposed to be the star of the show, is not much different. in fact, it is worse, because compared to her book 1 counterpart, she downgraded a lot. all her person does is either get sad about how she didnt want this destiny/prophecy/whatever and would rather look after sheep (which is what she actually said) or say “how dare you” to cyrus multiple times a day (or an hour, since, as you remember, the entire book is set during 1 day). i wish i could say i am exaggerating, but in fact i am not. i actually counted how many times she said “how dare you” throughout this book, and i invite you to take a guess before i tell you the answer.

16 times. i’ll give a few quotes below to showcase how ridiculous and irritating it got having to read it.

“How dare you,” she said. “You horrible cretin. You useless monster. How could you—”

“How dare you,” she said, her fists clenching.”

“How dare you slander my person when you know nothing about me—”

“How dare you,” she whispered.”

“I certainly will not listen to you— And how dare you call me stupid and infuriating—”

“She gasped. “I am not a demented Jinn, how dare you—”

okay girl, by now you must have gotten that cyrus, in fact, does dare to say that. now why cant you do something about it other than regurgitate the same nonsense hourly like a parrot?

speaking of cyrus, he is not much better than the other two. he is your typical, copy-paste love interest that one encounters in every “enemies” to lovers book nowadays. out-of-this-world attractive? check. sad backstory? check. snarky and sarcastic? check. the “i have actually been secretly in love with you for a long time and all of this enemies act has just been pretense for… uhhh… reasons” trope? check.

you would think that, for all its faults, this book would give us a good romance, since that is supposed to be the centerpiece of this series (and, truthfully, the reason why everyone is reading it in the first place). as you could probably guess, that was not the case for me lol. bland, drab and poorly written are the only descriptions i can conjure up for it. cyrus and alizeh were teased to be a “slowburn enemies to lovers” (to be fair, i dont remember where exactly this was mentioned, though i believe it was sometime before book 1 was published), but in what world can you actually stop hating your “enemy” after approximately 15 hours of finding out about his existence in the first place? she tried to murder him about 100 pages into the book, and in the evening of that same day she when he gets injured and starts bleeding. the bread that he bought her a couple of pages prior - the first kind thing he does for her so far - must have been exquisite, for her to react like that. i know that the romantasy is not exactly known for executing the e2l trope well, but the author didnt even try to do it here, which is just sad (for her).

to sum up my opinion on the romance, i can only say that it is as dull and unimaginative (another side note: can you tell i am trying really hard to come up with synonyms for ‘boring’?) as the characters themselves are, which should come off as no surprise, really.

lastly, i would like to tackle the nonexistent plot. earlier today, i was ranting about this novel to my friend, and when she asked me what the plot is even about, i realized that i could not answer. is it alizeh becoming the queen of jinn? maybe. alizeh & co fighting the devil? perhaps. there are bits and pieces here and there but no one big, exciting plot that would make this whole story worth reading. were this book 1, it wouldnt be a problem as the story would still be in its early stages. however, it is already the 2nd installment in the series, and such questions should have been answered by now. it is possible that the author may have wanted to focus on romance rather than the plot, but if that’s the case then… i have already made my opinion on the romance aspect known.

⚠︎ Warning: The events of this book in question take place over a single day. Yes. A. Single. Day. So tread into this series with caution for you might fall head over heels over ONE day ⚠︎

: ̗̀➛ 🅞🅝🅔 🅓🅐🅨 🅣🅞 🅕🅔🅔🅛 🅘🅣 🅐🅛🅛: Call it baloney, call me biased.

But I think it’s wrong to expect too much plot from the second book of any trilogy or series. It’s granted that the second book should act as a bridge between the exposition of the starter and the explosion of the finale.

That is to say, this book is purely vibes and gosh am I be vibing (ᴗ_ᴗ.)

Translation: I’m a simpleminded bitch and I justify the wrongs of things I love ∘ ∘ ∘ ( °ヮ° ) ?

Here I was smitten by the first book. And even then Tahereh Mafi brought out the big guns in this one.

The fantasy elements were heavenly.

The prose, decadent.

The word-building, absolutely monumental.

Everything about this book screamed GRAND and EXQUISITE and I’m damned if I say otherwise. I was content in closing my eyes after every random description and let it form in my imaginings because I cannot remember the last time any type of beautiful writing gave me this wild a thrill:

“The heaviness of night drew back in an unhurried reveal, inches of dark pleating away not unlike curtains on a stage. An audience of one stood impatient before the sight, waiting with bated breath for the set dressing of the next scene, the next act in her life.”


If this is how one perceives a sunrise of all things, then I’m certain Tahereh Mafi was born a poet. Apart from this, I can’t think of any logical explanation other than me being an uncultured heathen!

: ̗̀➛ 🅞🅝🅔 🅓🅐🅨 🅣🅞 🅑🅔🅒🅞🅜🅔 🅐 🅢🅘🅜🅟 (𝔸𝕝𝕚𝕫𝕖𝕙 𝔼𝕕𝕚𝕥𝕚𝕠𝕟): Oh Alizeh, forget Kamran and Cyrus. Marry me, I’m clearly the better option ( •᷄ᴗ•́)

My love, admiration and respect for Alizeh know no bounds. This girl is, by far the biggest miracle I’ve witnessed. She’s soft, but steely. She’s sweet, but shrewd. She’ll pluck the stars out of the heavens to make you smile. But she’s also capable of making you kneel before her and cry for mercy if you try something funny. She’s the biggest bookish paradox and boy do I scream HELL YEAH!

Finally an FMC who unabashedly loves the lovely pretty things, who appreciates dazzling dresses, romantic regalia and FLOWERS, ahh flowers.

“You strike me as precisely the sort of maudlin person who would appreciate the company of flowers while crying.”


Again, what the hell is wrong with me that I make a big deal out of FLOWERS? Clearly, something is wrong with YOU if you don’t appreciate flowers It’s a small pleasure seeing the FMC not shying away from stereotypically girly things as is the popular trend albeit how little these mentions may be. She’s ridiculously precious, and a jewel for that ♡

UGH SHE MAKES ME SO SAPPY

And in the next breath she’s also saying things like this:

“A gentleman? Do you often confuse yourself for such a man?”


#Grill&RoastMenForSupper ᕙ( •̀ ᗜ •́ )ᕗ

When asked, “If you could befriend one fictional character, who would it be?”, you can find me rolling on the floor, screaming, crying, throwing up, “ALL HAIL QUEEN ALIZEH!”

: ̗̀➛ 🅞🅝🅔 🅓🅐🅨 🅣🅞 🅑🅔🅒🅞🅜🅔 🅐 🅢🅘🅜🅟 (ℂ𝕪𝕣𝕦𝕤 𝔼𝕕𝕚𝕥𝕚𝕠𝕟): I didn’t realise my heart was such a faulty organ until I read this book. Pray tell, why else would I BLUSH at something like this?

“Try to weaponize those eyes against me again and I will have them permanently sewn shut.”


No, please answer.

It is not normal for me to to feel flustered at shit like this, I swear! ヽ༼ ಥ_ಥ༽ﾉ

“When you threatened just hours ago to have my eyes sewn shut?”

He looked sharply away from her then, a muscle jumping in his jaw. “I shouldn’t have said that.”

“And then you threw me off a cliff,” she said, her voice a bit breathless even to her own ears.

“You wouldn’t stop threatening to kill me,” he said angrily, turning back to face her. “I was merely trying to change the subject.”

“By having me devoured by dragons?” she nearly cried.


Ladies and gentlemen, I present to you all: the REAL enemies to lovers (◍•ᴗ•◍)

“Tell me—is it too much to hope for our future that you will not make it a habit of slapping me in the face?”

“Yes.”

“I see. Then married life will be exactly as I imagined.”


Shut up, young man! You are not allowed to make me snort like that ×͜×

Cyrus broke through that armour I put on. I refuse to be swayed THIS easily by his charms. When I tell you, I high-pitch-squealed my way through all his scenes, you should know that I don’t say it LIGHTLY-

“Of all the trials I’ve recently endured,” he said, turning his face up to the sky. “You are by far the most excruciating.”

ㅤ ‍‍‍‍‍‍ ‍‍‍‍‍‍ ‍‍‍‍‍‍ ‍‍‍‍‍‍˗ˏˋ★‿︵‧ ˚ ₊⊹ short summary
ㅤ ‍‍‍‍‍‍ "These Infinite Threads" by Tahereh Mafi is a gorgeously written, emotionally rich sequel that elevates everything from the first book. The prose is vivid and lyrical, steeped in imagery that feels almost otherworldly, and the story pulses with poetic weight and quiet intensity.

ㅤ ‍‍‍‍‍‍ At the heart of it all is Alizeh and Cyrus (yes, I am choosing to ignore Kamran)—two powerful, stubborn forces caught in a tangled web of fate, politics, and painful choices. Their dynamic crackles with tension, not just romantic but existential, as both wrestle with who they are, what they’ve lost, and what they might become. The emotional depth is immense, and their internal monologues are hauntingly beautiful—filled with yearning, grief, and razor-sharp reflection. It's a story that aches in all the right places.


ㅤ ‍‍‍‍‍‍ ‍‍‍‍‍‍ ‍‍‍‍‍‍ ‍‍‍‍‍‍˗ˏˋ★‿︵‧ ˚ ₊⊹ honest thoughts
ㅤ ‍‍‍‍‍‍ ⋅ ☾ I feel like I don't even have genuine thoughts after this book, but as I also mentioned previously for This Woven Kingdom I am absolutely in love with the magnificent writing in this book. I simply could not put this book down because of how eager I was to just read one more line of these perfectly crafted words, just one more paragraph of another magnificently vivid imagery. I am simply addicted to this world.

ㅤ ‍‍‍‍‍‍ ⋅ ☾ The more I read into this series, the more I realise that my dissatisfaction with the plot importance from the first book was slightly misguided. This is a series that definitely does not focus on plot, but rather on its characters, on their oh, so consuming feelings and experiences and it definitely focuses on emotion. Therefore, it would be unwise of me to keep judging it for something it is definitely not meant to focus on. It does an absolutely exquisite job at portraying such powerful feelings that you end up experiencing everything yourself.

ㅤ ‍‍‍‍‍‍ ⋅ ☾ This book genuinely felt like a magnificently crafted dream. From the gorgeous world to the gut-wrenching monologues of the characters, this was simply a piece of art for me. I genuinely did not mind the lack of a very developed and strong plot, because I was so caught up in everything else this book has presented me with that I, honestly, simply had no time to mind anything else.

ㅤ ‍‍‍‍‍‍ ⋅ ☾ I want to sincerely apologise for my lack of judgement because I dared to think that the romance in this book shall be just as inconspicuous and annoying insignificant in terms of emotional depth in a similar manner to the first book; because I was so wrong about this. The romance in this book, especially in what concerns the second half of the book, will be the cause of many heart and sleep issues for me in the future.
ㅤ ‍‍‍‍‍‍ I am safe to say, I was not expecting anything from what came for me in the very last part of the book. I was definitely not expecting to have my heart shattered to pieces by such incredibly passionate and painful confessions. But I am afraid this book managed to completely ruin me with its beauty and incredible writing when it comes to love.

ㅤ ‍‍‍‍‍‍ ⋅ ☾ Something this book does so incredibly amazing is keeping such a general state of mystery and confusion which you are forced to endure together with the characters. And due to this, even though the ending of this book is not some shocking cliff-hanger, you are still left craving more and desperate to just keep reading the next one. The ending of this book almost did not allow me to sleep peacefully at night unless I started the next book as soon as possible.
ㅤ ‍‍‍‍‍‍ I was left speechless and so frustrated with the incredibly cruel fate the characters seem to be forced to endure and, in exchange, I AM FORCED TO ENDURE TOO!


ㅤ ‍‍‍‍‍‍ ‍‍‍‍‍‍ ‍‍‍‍‍‍ ‍‍‍‍‍‍˗ˏˋ★‿︵‧ ˚ ₊⊹ characters
ㅤ ‍‍‍‍‍‍These characters managed to become so insanely dear to me (not you, Kamran) and I am genuinely shocked about how much I came to care for them (not you, Kamran) and to empathise with them in such a short period of time (not you, Kamran).

ㅤ ‍‍‍‍‍‍ ✧ Alizeh - Despite still being able to see the kindness in her in the first book as well, I feel like her innocence and pure heart really managed to shine in this one. There is strenght in kindness and delicacy and Alizeh, as a character, really manages to show that perfectly. I loved how her interactions from the first book mostly managed to emphasize her strenght, while her interactions with Cyrus made her innocent and young side shine in the most beautiful, fun and emotionally charged banter. I am really looking forward to her progress and this duality of her character in the next books. All I can say for now is that I absolutely love her.

ㅤ ‍‍‍‍‍‍ ✧ Cyrus - The man I was waiting for ever since the ending of the first book. I never thought I would say this, but Jacks definitely finally found his competition in this man. Since I was finding his character fun and sassy at first, I was expecting lots of banter and entertaining fights between him and Alizeh. What I DID NOT expect was for my heart to shatter entirely for this man, to feel such a deep and gruesome heartbreak for him and to fall so deeply in love with his confessions. This man is the sheer definition of yearning. I have never met a man who literally acts like his world is ending once the woman he loves is out of his reach.
ㅤ ‍‍‍‍‍‍ Believe me when I say, there is no way for this man to not become your next obsession. I know for sure he defnitely became mine.

ㅤ ‍‍‍‍‍‍ ✧ Kamran - I hate this man too much to give him the honour of receiving a proper opinion from my end. Imagine a man that is so entitled and so desperate to be loved that he goes on and meets a person, creates an image of that person for himself in his own mind, falls in love with that image and then goes on to somehow demand that person to love him back. You can draw your own opinions about him from here. All I say is that this man is NOT in love and definitely does not deserve my pity.

ㅤ ‍‍‍‍‍‍ ✧ Hazan - You're still doing so amazing, sweety. I absolutely love you with my entire heart. ❤️

ㅤ ‍‍‍‍‍‍ ✧ Sarra - You can take Kamran's hand and go and be psychos together in peace.


ㅤ ‍‍‍‍‍‍ ‍‍‍‍‍‍ ‍‍‍‍‍‍ ‍‍‍‍‍‍˗ˏˋ★‿︵‧ ˚ ₊⊹ should you read this?
ㅤ ‍‍‍‍‍‍ To genuinely reply this, I am going to embark on my self-imposed quest of convincing everybody I know to read this book and demand of them to pick this up and start reading it. Therefore, the short answer is yes, you should be reading this. I am genuinely absolutely mesmerised by the writing of this entire series and when you pair this with characters of such beautiful craftmenship, I am bound to find myself, once again, in love with a book.
ㅤ ‍‍‍‍‍‍ Yes, I am already good into the next book while I am writing this because there was no way for me to stop reading.

──⟡⋆˙✩ 4.25 stars ✩ ⋆˙⟡──

This review contains spoilers from book one

After the last book ended with Cyrus going, “We getting married! Surprise, surprise!” of course, I had to immediately start this one to find out Alizeh’s answer (other than falling off the dragon in shock). And this is what I was greeted with:

⋆𐙚₊˚⊹♡ 𝐋𝐞𝐭 𝐦𝐞 𝐛𝐞 𝐩𝐥𝐚𝐢𝐧: 𝐈 𝐝𝐞𝐭𝐞𝐬𝐭 𝐲𝐨𝐮. 𝐈 𝐰𝐨𝐮𝐥𝐝 𝐬𝐨𝐨𝐧𝐞𝐫 𝐢𝐧𝐠𝐞𝐬𝐭 𝐩𝐨𝐢𝐬𝐨𝐧 𝐭𝐡𝐚𝐧 𝐦𝐚𝐫𝐫𝐲 𝐲𝐨𝐮.

Ahem.

On the flip side—enemies to lovers?

Because in the beginning, Cyrus is all, “Now listen here, girlie. I don’t wanna marry you, but I have to ‘cause the devil ordered me to. Don’t think I’ll fall for your pretty eyes like Kamran over there. I’m a big, scary, mean, heartless boy!”

To which Alizeh is like:

⋆𐙚₊˚⊹♡ "𝐈 𝐭𝐫𝐮𝐥𝐲 𝐡𝐚𝐭𝐞 𝐲𝐨𝐮," 𝐬𝐡𝐞 𝐰𝐡𝐢𝐬𝐩𝐞𝐫𝐞𝐝, 𝐡𝐞𝐫 𝐯𝐨𝐢𝐜𝐞 𝐭𝐡𝐢𝐜𝐤 𝐰𝐢𝐭𝐡 𝐞𝐦𝐨𝐭𝐢𝐨𝐧. "𝐖𝐢𝐭𝐡 𝐦𝐲 𝐰𝐡𝐨𝐥𝐞 𝐡𝐞𝐚𝐫𝐭, 𝐈 𝐡𝐚𝐭𝐞 𝐲𝐨𝐮."

This reader: JUMPS AND SQUEALS AND GIGGLES I need help

˚₊· ͟͟͞͞➳❥ Would you believe me if I said this entire book spans over one day? No? Well, it does. T_T Like, the book starts at night and ends the next night. Everything Alizeh and Cyrus go through—the transitions from hatred to friendliness to catching feelings, back to hatred again on the last page, to becoming allies and is your head spinning? mine too

˚₊· ͟͟͞͞➳❥ Cyrus is not what I expected. And I’m sorry for being useless, but I genuinely cannot give you an opinion on him yet. I haven’t even decided on one myself. I don’t know... he’s so weird. Like, I don’t know what to think of him. He’s this bizarre mix of cruel and soft, of suffering himself and causing suffering in return. He says mean things, yet he’s oddly sensitive to them. And he’s skittish. So skittish. So suspicious. He reminded me of my parrot—when feeling cornered, he’d bite at everyone and everything, regardless of whether they meant him harm.

Talking about my feelings towards him, I believe my perception of him developed alongside Alizeh’s. Both of our hearts kept softening toward him because, at times, he felt like a scared, lost boy. But then we’d remember how dangerous he was—how he would lie and trick under the devil’s orders. Because yes, as we know from book one, he struck a deal with Iblees and now must do his bidding... or suffer the consequences.

˚₊· ͟͟͞͞➳❥ As for Alizeh—why is she so loveable? I’m not kidding. She’s both pookie-coded and a badass queen. I didn’t even think that was possible! One of my absolute favorite things about her is that she knows when to take a stand. Compassion is such a huge part of her, yet she’s careful not to let it cloud her judgment or make her susceptible to manipulation. She ensures it doesn’t turn into a weakness—something others can push her around with. And that’s just so admirable to me because I rarely see this kind of balance in books.

˚₊· ͟͟͞͞➳❥ To those of you who suffer from life’s unpredictability and ever-changing nature, fear not! There is one thing in life that is constant: these damn Kamran POVs.

Now, don’t get me wrong—I have nothing against the boy. But do I really have to be in his head? Is it absolutely necessary? Truly?

This book would have been half its size without the Kamran chapters, and I’m SO ANNOYED!

did this entire four hundred page book span only two days? yes. did basically nothing happen during those two days? also yes. did i still absolutely love this? undeniably yes.

cyrus de nara the most yearning yearner who has ever yearned.

"You have no idea what I want. I have been in agony for eight months, Alizeh. Do you know how hard it’s been to pretend I don’t know you? To pretend I don’t want you? To act as if I haven’t known every inch of your body in my dreams? To learn that your heart has been entangled elsewhere? I look at you and I can’t breathe. In my mind, you are already mine."

"God, you’re so beautiful,” he said, his smile vanishing. “Even when you lie to me.”

“Your name,” he said, and closed his eyes. He nearly fell over, catching himself at the last second. “I didn’t know your name for so long, angel. I love the way it feels in my mouth.”

“I would marry you,” he said, stepping closer again, coming dangerously within reach. “I’d marry you tomorrow. And then I’d take you to bed. For weeks.”

“You act as if I’m intentionally cruel. As if I’m indifferent to you.” “Aren’t you?” “No,” she whispered, her eyes filling with tears. “Of course not.” Cyrus stared at her from where he stood, his chest heaving with barely leashed intensity. He devastated her with that look, even as he seemed planted in the ground, immovable. “Then be with me,” he said softly. “Let me worship you.”

“My kingdom," he said softly. "For your hand.”

“I hate you,” he whispered. Alizeh blinked, her heart pounding too hard in her chest. “I know.” He leaned in then, his throat working, his gaze fixed entirely on her mouth. “I hate everything about you. Your eyes. Your lips. Your smile.” His words grazed her skin when he said, softly, “I find your presence insufferable.”
